column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbdillāh Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī (may Allah be pleased with them both): “A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: Do you think that if I pray the obligatory prayers, fast Ramaḍān,
treat the lawful as lawful and the unlawful as unlawful, and do nothing more than that, I will enter Paradise?
He said: Yes.” Reported by Muslim.
“That a man”: he was al-Nuʿmān ibn Qawqal, and it is said someone else. A-raʾayta (“do you think”): tell me.
Al-maktūbāt (“the obligatory prayers”): the five prescribed prayers.
“And fast Ramaḍān”: refrain during its days from whatever breaks the fast, with an intention.
“Treat the lawful as lawful”: do it believing it to be lawful.
“And the unlawful as unlawful”: avoid it, believing it to be unlawful.
“And do nothing more than that”: of voluntary deeds.
“Will I enter Paradise?”: will I deserve to enter Paradise?
Naʿam (“yes”): you will enter Paradise.
Whoever carries out the obligations and refrains from what is unlawful enters Paradise.
It is permissible to leave voluntary deeds if it is not out of carelessness and disregard for them.
Considering people's circumstances: perhaps the questioner was new to Islam, so it was made easy for him until his faith grew strong.
The great importance of the five prayers, fasting Ramaḍān, treating the lawful as lawful and avoiding the unlawful.
Avoiding the unlawful and consuming the lawful brings about the reform of the individual and of society.
If this hadith were acted upon, security would be established,
trust between people would grow strong,
and disputes and quarrels between them would cease. But how far, how far that is!

The Companion Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him) tells us in this hadith that a man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the form of a question, showing that he would act on whatever the Messenger ﷺ guided him to.
He said: Tell me, if I keep up the five prayers, fast the whole month of Ramaḍān, believe that the lawful is lawful to consume and use,
and that the unlawful is unlawful, believing it to be unlawful and avoiding it,
and do nothing more of voluntary deeds than what I have asked you about,
will I be among those who deserve to enter Paradise?

The Prophet ﷺ said to him: Yes, you will enter Paradise. He did not mention Ḥajj and zakāh, either because they were not obligatory on the questioner, or because they are included in the lawful, or because they had not yet been made obligatory when he asked.
Indeed, in the prayer lies all good and all virtue, / for through it the necks bow down in submission.
It was the first duty prescribed in our religion, / and the last thing to remain when the religion is lifted.
